title: Mandakini on Ram Teri Ganga Maili at 41: 'I Went With the Flow'
excerpt: Four decades after Raj Kapoor's 1985 classic made her a star, the actress has reflected on the film's controversial scenes, telling The Indian Express's Expresso series that as a young newcomer she simply trusted her director and followed his vision.
body:
• Mandakini told The Indian Express's Expresso series that she "went with the flow" while shooting Raj Kapoor's Ram Teri Ganga Maili as a young newcomer.
  • The 1985 film, Kapoor's last directorial, turned 41 this year; Mandakini marked the anniversary in August with a week of behind-the-scenes memories on Instagram.
  • She has previously defended the controversial waterfall and breastfeeding sequences as "pure" rather than exploitative, contrasting them with the sensuality of today's screen.
  • She recalled Kapoor wanted a "fresh face" for the role — "how can I make someone pure Ganga if they have an established image?" — and addressed Padmini Kolhapure's claim that Kapoor had approached her for the part.

Forty-one years after Ram Teri Ganga Maili made her an overnight sensation, Mandakini has looked back at the film that defined her career — and the controversial scenes that defined the conversation around it — telling The Indian Express's Expresso series that she simply went with the flow.

The reflection

Cast by Raj Kapoor as a debutante in his 1985 romantic drama, Mandakini played Ganga, an innocent village girl whose life unravels after she is abandoned. The film became one of the biggest hits of the decade, but its legacy was complicated by two sequences that drew intense scrutiny at the time: Mandakini bathing in a waterfall in a transparent white saree, and a sequence suggesting her character breastfeeding her newborn.

Speaking to Expresso, the actress framed her experience as that of a young newcomer who trusted her director's vision. "I went with the flow," she said — a striking understatement for a performance that generated decades of debate.

"It was also a pure form"

Mandakini has addressed the controversy before. In a throwback interaction with Hindustan Times, she pushed back against the way the breastfeeding sequence has been remembered. "It was not a breastfeeding scene, it was shot in such a way that it could look like one," she said, adding that what appeared on screen was achieved technically.

"It was not a breastfeeding scene, it was shot in such a way that it could look like one. If I go on to explain how it was done, it would be too long (a story). It (her scene) was also a pure form. Nowadays, it is all about sexuality."

— Mandakini, to Hindustan Times

She drew a sharp contrast between the 1985 film and contemporary screen sensuality, arguing that the earlier scenes were presented in a pure form while "nowadays, it is all about sexuality."

Why Kapoor chose her

Mandakini has recalled that Kapoor wanted a fresh face for the role. In a separate interview with Pinkvilla, she remembered their first meeting: Kapoor was happy to see her in Indian attire and said he wanted somebody homely. "How can I make someone pure Ganga if they have an established image?" he told her, she recalled.

The casting was not without its own drama. Padmini Kolhapure later claimed that Kapoor had approached her for the role even after shooting with Mandakini for 45 days. Mandakini said she was unaware of any such approach, noting only that "everyone wanted to take up the role." Kolhapure, for her part, said she declined because she was not comfortable with a kissing scene — and that the controversial sequences were never part of the film when she was in discussions.

Forty-one years on

The film turned 41 in August, and Mandakini marked the moment by dedicating a week on Instagram to Ram Teri Ganga Maili, sharing behind-the-scenes stories and inviting fans to ask questions about the shoot — locations, anecdotes and memories she said had never been shared before. "Even after all these years, I continue to receive memories, stories and questions related to the film," she wrote.

Life after Ganga

No later role matched the impact of her debut. She went on to star in films including Dance Dance and Pyaar Karke Dekho, but by the mid-1990s her film career had wound down; she left the industry after Zordaar in 1996. She married Dr. Kagyur T. Rinpoche Thakur, denied reports linking her to Dawood Ibrahim, and laughed off an old rumour — revived on The Kapil Sharma Show — that her father had shot her.

In 2022 she made a comeback of sorts in the music video "Maa O Maa," appearing alongside her son Rabbil Thakur. Four decades on, the Expresso interview suggests she has made her peace with the film that made her famous — and with the flow she chose to go with.
image_caption: Actor Mandakini. She starred in Raj Kapoor's Ram Teri Ganga Maili, which turned 41 this year.
nri_angle: For the diaspora generation that grew up watching the film on VHS tapes and cable reruns, the Expresso conversation is a nostalgic re-examination of a film whose most famous scenes overshadowed everything else about it.
